t.1.39.1: Having heard the words of the gods, the blessed Grandfather replied to them, who were sorely terrified and bewildered by the power of Death.
t.1.39.2: The wise Vāsudeva, to whom this entire earth belongs, assumes the form of Kapila and ceaselessly upholds the earth.
t.1.39.3: The splitting open of the earth has indeed been foreseen as something eternally ordained, and so too the destruction of the short-lived sons of Sagara.
t.1.39.4: Having heard the words of the Grandfather, O tamer of foes, the thirty-three gods, supremely delighted, went back again the way they had come.
t.1.39.5: And as the earth was being split open by the great-souled sons of Sagara, there arose a sound like the crash of a thunderbolt.
t.1.39.6: Then, having split open the whole earth and also having circumambulated it, all the Sagaras together spoke these words to their father.
t.1.39.7: The whole earth has been traversed, and mighty beings have been slain: gods, Dānavas, Rākṣasas, Piśācas, serpents and Kiṃnaras.
t.1.39.8: We see neither that horse nor the one who stole the horse. What shall we do? May good fortune be with you; let a plan be considered in this matter.
t.1.39.9: Having heard those words of his sons, O Raghunandana, Sagara, best of kings, spoke these words in anger.
t.1.39.10: Dig further, and may good fortune be with you! Having split open the surface of the earth and found the thief of the horse, you will return with your purpose accomplished.
t.1.39.11: Abiding by the word of their father, the great-souled Sagara, the sixty thousand sons rushed toward Rasātala.
t.1.39.13: O delight of the Raghus, the great elephant Virūpākṣa bore upon his head the entire earth together with its mountains and forests.
t.1.39.12: Then, as it was being dug, they saw the elephant of the quarter, Virūpākṣa, huge as a mountain, holding up the surface of the earth.
t.1.39.14: O Kākutstha, when at the turning of the seasons that great elephant, out of weariness, shakes its head to rest, then an earthquake occurs.
t.1.39.15: Having circumambulated that great elephant, the guardian of the quarter, and paying him honour, they went on, O Rāma, breaking through Rasātala.
t.1.39.16: Then, having broken through the eastern quarter, they broke through the southern one again; and in the southern quarter too they saw a mighty elephant.
t.1.39.17: Seeing the great-souled Mahāpadma, like a very great mountain, bearing the earth upon his head, they were struck with the utmost wonder.
t.1.39.18: Then, having made a circumambulation, the sixty thousand sons of the great-souled Sagara broke open the western quarter.
t.1.39.19: In the western direction too, those mighty ones beheld the huge elephant of the quarter, Saumanasa, who was like a mountain.
t.1.39.20: Having circumambulated him and asked after his well-being, they then went on digging and advanced toward the quarter belonging to Soma.
t.1.39.21: In the northern quarter, O best of the Raghus, they saw Bhadra, white as snow, bearing this earth with his auspicious body.
t.1.39.22: Then all of them, the sixty thousand sons, having touched him and walked around him in reverent circumambulation, split open the surface of the earth.
t.1.39.23: Then, having gone to the renowned north-eastern quarter, all the Sāgaras, the sons of Sagara, dug into the earth out of anger.
t.1.39.24: There they saw Kapila, the eternal Vāsudeva, and, grazing not far from that god, the horse.
t.1.39.25: Recognizing him as the destroyer of the sacrifice, they, their eyes agitated with wrath, rushed at him in fury and cried, "Stop! Stop!"
t.1.39.26: It is you who have stolen our sacrificial horse! O fool, know that we who have come here are the sons of Sagara.
t.1.39.27: Having heard those words of theirs, O Raghunandana, Kapila, seized by great fury, then uttered the sound "hum."
t.1.39.28: Then, O Kākutstha, all the sons of Sagara were reduced to heaps of ashes by that immeasurable, great-souled Kapila.
